desc:
A version string is a list of non-negative integers called revisions, written in decimal and separated by single dots, for example "1.02.7". A revision may have leading zeros, which do not change its value (02 is the number 2).

Compare v1 and v2 revision by revision from left to right. The first position where the revision values differ decides: return -1 if v1 is smaller there, 1 if it is larger. If one version has fewer revisions, the missing ones count as 0. If all revisions are equal, return 0.

Examples: "1.01" and "1.001" are equal (0); "1.0" and "1.0.0.0" are equal (0); "0.9" versus "0.10" gives -1 because 9 < 10.
constraints: Each version consists of digits and dots; there is at least one digit between two dots and no dot at either end
Every revision has at most 9 digits
hints: Comparing the two strings with ordinary string comparison fails: "9" is larger than "10" as text.
Split each version at the dots and turn every revision into an integer, so leading zeros disappear.
Walk both lists up to the longer length, using 0 when a list has run out. Return at the first difference. You can also do this with two pointers and no split, parsing one revision at a time.
editorial: Parse the revisions one at a time with two pointers. For each version, read digits until the next dot or the end of the string and accumulate the value x = x * 10 + digit; when a version is already exhausted its revision is 0. Compare the two numbers: if they differ, the answer is -1 or 1, otherwise skip the dots and continue. The loop runs until both versions are exhausted.

Padding with zeros is what makes 1.0 equal to 1.0.0. A common bug is to stop at the shorter version and then decide by length, which wrongly calls 1.0.1 and 1.0 the same or 1.0.0 larger than 1. Time is linear in the total length and only O(1) extra space is needed with the pointer method.
solution:
def compareVersions(v1, v2):
    i = j = 0
    n, m = len(v1), len(v2)
    while i < n or j < m:
        x = 0
        while i < n and v1[i] != ".":
            x = x * 10 + ord(v1[i]) - 48
            i += 1
        y = 0
        while j < m and v2[j] != ".":
            y = y * 10 + ord(v2[j]) - 48
            j += 1
        if x != y:
            return -1 if x < y else 1
        i += 1
        j += 1
    return 0
